title: Prevent OpenCode wrapper tools from escaping mutation enforcement
description:
## Summary
Original bug: wrappers whose outer name/args lacked mutation tokens were allowed. Current plugin denies undeclared wrappers (`interactive_bash`, `skill_mcp`, `task`) via exact-ID fail-closed. Direct `custom_mutator` also denies.

## Remaining policy mistake in the old AC
"Read-only wrapper operations remain available" is not implemented and should **not** be implemented for undeclared IDs. Official OpenCode docs say `tool.execute.before` runs before every tool execution, so a later nested `write` can be intercepted — but `interactive_bash`/tmux can mutate without a nested OpenCode write. Parsing `tmux_command` or `skill_mcp.arguments` is a new heuristic, not a capability.

## What to keep
- Deny undeclared wrappers in clean state and repair (already tested in `_FAIL_CLOSED_TOOL_CASES` and `test_pending_repair_blocks_opaque_wrappers`).
- Keep declared `skill` available (skill loader, not `skill_mcp`).
- Do not add `task`/`skill_mcp`/`interactive_bash` to `READ_ONLY_TOOL_IDS`.

## Unproven invariant
Nested interception is not proven in-repo. Treat outer allow of an undeclared wrapper as an escape even if we *hope* a later hook fires.
design:
Choose option A from the original fork: deny undeclared wrappers at the hard gate. Do not recursively classify delegated operations from arguments.

Positive cases: declared `skill` (and other `READ_ONLY_TOOL_IDS`) remain available.
Negative cases: `interactive_bash`, `skill_mcp`, `task` deny in clean state and REPAIR_REQUIRED with the unknown-effect or repair-required error.

If a future wrapper is trusted, add its exact ID to the capability frozensets with a comment naming why; do not infer safety from the absence of mutation words.
acceptance_criteria: Undeclared wrappers cannot execute in clean state or REPAIR_REQUIRED. Declared `skill` remains available. End-to-end tests exist for `interactive_bash`, `skill_mcp`, and `task` (deny) and `skill` (allow). No decision parses wrapper payloads for nested mutation. No undeclared wrapper is allowlisted as "read-only".
notes: Citations: plugin 601-603; control-contract 73-90, 251-271, 409-418; OpenCode before-hook: https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/. Blocked by `slopgate-nvz.3`. Rejected: recursive MCP/task argument inspection.
close_reason: Covered opaque wrappers as denied and declared skill as allowed without recursive argument parsing.

title: Restore strict OpenCode REPAIR_REQUIRED gating
description:
## Summary
Original bug: `isAllowedWhileRepairRequired` treated "not a lexical filesystem mutation" as repair-safe. That is gone. The plugin now allowlists declared read-only IDs, `write`/`edit`/`apply_patch`, `slopgate_verify_repair`, and an exact `slopgate lint check` command.

## Policy conflict
This ticket's old acceptance text said only read-only + explicit repair/verify may run. That contradicts:
- README:148 (documents the deadlock exception)
- `REPAIR_MUTATION_TOOLS` in `src/slopgate/resources/opencode_plugin.ts` 153
- `tests/integration/test_opencode_plugin_repair_gate.py::test_pending_repair_allows_direct_file_repair_tool`

Reconciled policy: keep the approved deadlock exception. Do not re-tighten to read-only-only.

## Remaining gaps
1. Acceptance/docs/tests must all state the same allowlist.
2. Python/replay/daemon have no PreToolUse repair gate. `_record_opencode_repair_required` (`src/slopgate/engine/_evaluation.py` 42-81) only marks/clears repair after PostToolUse. A direct `evaluate_payload` call during REPAIR_REQUIRED will not emit the plugin's repair denial.
3. Declared remotes (`github_update_issue`, `api_delete_resource`) must stay blocked in repair (they are effectful, not in `REPAIR_MUTATION_TOOLS`). Untested.
4. Compound `slopgate lint check && ...` is already denied; keep that.
design:
Keep pending-repair policy independent from clean-state compatibility, but encode the approved exception explicitly:

Allow while REPAIR_REQUIRED:
- `READ_ONLY_TOOL_IDS`
- `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`
- `slopgate_verify_repair`
- `bash` whose command tokens are exactly `slopgate lint check` plus `--details`/`--verbose`

Deny: unknown IDs, wrappers, declared remotes, compound/suffixed shell, shell aliases (`powershell`, `pwsh`, `cmd`, `sh`, `zsh`, `shell`, `local_shell`, `terminal`).

Implement the same predicate in Python if replay/daemon/compat must match the plugin; otherwise document plugin-only repair gating and add a negative test that `evaluate_payload` does not claim to enforce it. Preserve generation matching and same/separate-worktree isolation (`tests/test_hook_state_scope.py`).
acceptance_criteria: While REPAIR_REQUIRED, the generated plugin allows only declared read-only IDs, write/edit/apply_patch, slopgate_verify_repair, and exact `slopgate lint check` (optional --details/--verbose). Unknown tools, wrappers, declared remotes, and compound shell are denied. Error text matches that policy. Same-worktree sharing, separate-worktree isolation, and generation matching stay green. Python/replay/daemon either implement the same allowlist or have an explicit documented/tested limitation. README matches.
notes: Citations: plugin 456-479, 592-599; README:148; `tests/integration/test_opencode_plugin_repair_gate.py`; control-contract repair tests 222-307. Do not implement the stale "read-only only" AC.
close_reason: Implemented matching Python/plugin REPAIR_REQUIRED allowlists and exact repair command policy.

title: Unify OpenCode tool-effect classification across TypeScript and Python
description:
## Summary
This is the remaining P0. Live plugin decisions are exact-ID. Python `OC-PROJECTION-001` still has a wider allow path.

## Divergence
`unresolved_opencode_projection_finding` (`projector.py` 194-203) returns None when any of:
- `is_read_only_tool_use` — intent names include `read_file`, `ripgrep`, `rg`, `lookat`, `look_at` (`_intent.py` 28-40) that are **not** in `READ_ONLY_TOOL_IDS`
- `is_shell_tool` — `sh`, `zsh`, `powershell`, `pwsh`, `power_shell`, `cmd`, `cmd.exe`, `command_prompt`, `shell`, `local_shell`, `terminal` (`_basic.py` 89-102)
- `opencode_tool_capability` is READ_ONLY
- status `unsupported` and capability EFFECTFUL

Generated TypeScript only substitutes the two frozensets and treats `bash` as the sole declared shell (`EFFECTFUL_TOOL_IDS` uses `BASH_TOOL_LOWER`).

## Reproduction
1. `evaluate_payload` with `tool_name=powershell` or `read_file` and unsupported projection => no `OC-PROJECTION-001` (Python allow).
2. Same names through the rendered plugin => `unknown OpenCode tool effect` (TS deny).
3. No single fixture is executed through Python, generated Bun plugin, handle, replay, and daemon.

## Impact
Replay/daemon/compat can allow tools the installed plugin would block, and tests can go green on one runtime only.
design:
One machine-readable contract: `src/slopgate/opencode_tool_capabilities.py`.

1. Delete the `is_read_only_tool_use` and `is_shell_tool` early-returns from `unresolved_opencode_projection_finding`. Keep those helpers for other rules; they are cross-platform intent, not the OpenCode hard gate.
2. Continue generating plugin sets from the same frozensets (`render_opencode_plugin`).
3. Add a shared fixture table `(tool, args, repair_state, expected_decision, runtime)` executed by at least generated Bun plugin and Python `evaluate_payload`. Handle/replay/daemon can consume the same table.
4. Normalize only exact lowercase ID (`opencode_tool_capability` already strips/lowers). Do not add dotted-name or MCP-prefix collapsing unless a fixture proves OpenCode actually emits that ID and we choose to declare it.
5. A contract test must fail if either runtime diverges from the table.
acceptance_criteria: Every shared fixture produces the same allow/block result in generated TypeScript and Python. `powershell`/`pwsh`/`cmd`/`sh`/`zsh`/`shell`/`read_file`/`ripgrep` are denied unless explicitly added to the capability frozensets. `bash` remains the only declared shell. Plugin placeholders stay generated from the Python sets. A contract test fails on divergence. Valid declared projection behavior is unchanged.
notes: Citations: `projector.py` 194-203; `_basic.py` 89-115; `_intent.py` 28-40, 225-226; `opencode_tool_capabilities.py` 59-81; installer 196-205. This ticket blocks `.1`, `.4`, and `.6` so later rows do not encode two classifiers.
close_reason: Unified Python and generated-plugin exact-ID classification with shared executable parity coverage.

title: Block alternate-schema OpenCode filesystem mutations
description:
## Summary
Original bug: unknown-tool safety required a mutation token *and* a top-level file-target key, so ordinary write schemas passed. That fail-open path is gone on the generated plugin: undeclared IDs are denied by `isKnownEffectTool` before execution.

## Current state
Exact-ID denial already covers the original `custom_write` filename/paths/uri/nested-input cases and `mcp__docs__write({path})` in `tests/adapters/test_opencode_projection/test_engine.py` and `tests/integration/test_opencode_plugin_control_contract.py::_FAIL_CLOSED_TOOL_CASES`.

## Remaining gap
Executable coverage still omits literal rows named by the first audit:
- `mcpDocsWrite({filePath})`
- `mcp__docs__write({targetPath})`
- `files` / `target` / `destination` variants

These should deny because the *ID* is undeclared, not because a schema walker found a path. Invalid/stale/protocol-mismatch projections for declared `write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` are already tested in `test_engine.py` (`invalid-patch`, `invalid-edit`, `protocol-mismatch`, `test_stale_edit_projection_is_blocked`).

## Do not do
Do not add nested-argument or camelCase schema inspection as the trust boundary. That fights `slopgate-nvz.3` and reopens remote false positives (`slopgate-nvz.4`).
design:
Keep fail-closed exact-ID denial. Add the missing literal undeclared-ID rows to both the generated-plugin matrix and Python `evaluate_payload` matrix after `slopgate-nvz.3` removes Python's `is_read_only_tool_use`/`is_shell_tool` bypasses.

Benign pass-through remains declared IDs only (`gitnexus_context`, `skill`, `read`, etc. from `READ_ONLY_TOOL_IDS`). Schema normalization is not required for this ticket and should not be introduced here.
acceptance_criteria: Generated-plugin and Python-engine tests deny all original plus newly listed undeclared mutation IDs (`custom_write` filename/paths/uri/nested, `mcpDocsWrite(filePath)`, `mcp__docs__write(path|targetPath)`, files/target/destination) before execution because the ID is undeclared. Declared `gitnexus_context` and `skill` remain usable. Invalid/stale/protocol-mismatch projections for declared mutators remain blocked. No new path/schema heuristic is added. Focused and full tests pass.
notes: Citations: plugin `isKnownEffectTool` `src/slopgate/resources/opencode_plugin.ts` 482-488, 601-603; Python `unresolved_opencode_projection_finding` 180-214; existing rows `_FAIL_CLOSED_TOOL_CASES` and `_UNRESOLVED_MUTATIONS`. Blocked by `slopgate-nvz.3` so new rows are asserted against one classifier.

title: Restore safe OpenCode unknown-tool enforcement
description:
## Summary
The original fail-open leak (lexical mutation-token + top-level path-key) is already closed on the live OpenCode path. Remaining work is policy reconciliation, Python/plugin parity, executable evidence, and stopping any return to schema/path heuristics.

## Current architecture
Two gates exist:

1. Generated plugin hard gate in `src/slopgate/resources/opencode_plugin.ts` (`isAllowedWhileRepairRequired` 470-479, `isKnownEffectTool` 482-488, `tool.execute.before` 585-603). Unknown tools throw *before* `callEnforcer`.
2. Python second gate in `unresolved_opencode_projection_finding` (`src/slopgate/adapters/opencode_projection/projector.py` 180-214), injected by `evaluate_payload` (`src/slopgate/engine/_evaluation.py` 111-116). This path still bypasses the exact registry via `is_read_only_tool_use` and `is_shell_tool`.

Exact IDs live in `src/slopgate/opencode_tool_capabilities.py` and are substituted into the plugin by `render_opencode_plugin` (`src/slopgate/installer/_opencode.py` 182-213). Official OpenCode `tool.execute.before` only exposes `tool`, `sessionID`, `callID`, and mutable `output.args` — no provider/capability metadata ([plugins docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/)).

## Original reproductions (already closed on the plugin path)
`custom_write` alternate schemas, `interactive_bash`/`skill_mcp`/`task` wrappers, and undeclared tools now fail closed via exact-ID denial. `github_update_issue`/`api_delete_resource` are declared effectful IDs, so they are no longer false-positive local-mutation denials.

## Remaining blast radius
Python `evaluate_payload`, replay, daemon, and compat-handle can still disagree with the generated plugin. Repair ACs still contradict the approved deadlock exception. Contract-matrix evidence is a test-name grep, not a shared executable matrix.

## Child order
Do `slopgate-nvz.3` first. Then `.2` (policy + Python repair gate) in parallel with `.1`/`.6`/`.4` coverage. `slopgate-nvz.5` last.
design:
## Reconciled design (2026-08-22 research)

Keep exact declared IDs as the only trust boundary. Do not restore lexical mutation verbs, path-key presence, nested-argument walkers, or provider-provenance claims the OpenCode hook surface cannot supply.

### Trust model
- Source of truth: `READ_ONLY_TOOL_IDS` / `EFFECTFUL_TOOL_IDS` in `src/slopgate/opencode_tool_capabilities.py`.
- Plugin must receive those sets only through `render_opencode_plugin`.
- Python `OC-PROJECTION-001` must use `opencode_tool_capability()` only. Remove `is_read_only_tool_use` and `is_shell_tool` bypasses.
- Unknown / undeclared ID => deny. Declared read-only => allow through the hard gate. Declared effectful => forward to the engine (projection, rules).
- "Provenance" here means exact lowercase tool ID from Slopgate's registry, not MCP server identity. OpenCode's before-hook does not provide provider metadata.

### Repair policy (approved deadlock exception)
While `REPAIR_REQUIRED`, allow only:
- declared read-only IDs
- exact `write` / `edit` / `apply_patch`
- `slopgate_verify_repair`
- exact `bash` command `slopgate lint check` plus optional `--details`/`--verbose`

Deny declared remotes, wrappers, unknown tools, compound shell, and shell aliases. Plugin already implements this (`REPAIR_MUTATION_TOOLS` + `isExplicitRepairCommand`). Python currently has no PreToolUse repair gate (`_record_opencode_repair_required` is PostToolUse-only). Add the same allowlist to the Python/replay/daemon path or document that repair gating is plugin-only and test that limitation.

Do **not** re-tighten repair to read-only-only; that reintroduces the repair deadlock `tests/integration/test_opencode_plugin_repair_gate.py` locks in.

### Wrappers
Undeclared wrappers stay denied. Do not parse `tmux_command`, `skill_mcp.arguments`, or `task.prompt`. Nested `write`/`edit`/`bash` from a later OpenCode tool call can be independently intercepted, but `interactive_bash`/tmux can mutate outside that invariant. The read-only positive is declared `skill` / `gitnexus_*`, not hypothetical wrapper IDs.

### Remote effects
Declared effectful remotes stay available in clean state because they are declared IDs, not because their `path` looks remote. Unknown tools with path-like fields stay denied. During repair, declared remotes stay denied.

### Evidence
Replace matrix name-search (`tests/test_opencode_hook_contract_matrix.py` 54-69) with one shared fixture table executed by generated Bun plugin and Python `evaluate_payload` (handle/replay/daemon as follow-through). README:148 already states the exact-ID + repair-exception policy; keep docs no stronger than that.

### Rejected alternatives
- Schema inspection as trust boundary (reopens .1/.4).
- Recursive wrapper argument classification (unproven, spoofable).
- Python intent helpers as OpenCode allowlist (`read_file`, `ripgrep`, `powershell` are wider than the plugin).
- Claiming OpenCode permission parity; `permission.asked` is advisory and version-sensitive ([plugins docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/)). Platform capability remains degraded (`src/slopgate/engine/_runner.py` 86-90).
acceptance_criteria: Reconciled policy is recorded on the parent and children. Python and generated-plugin decisions match a shared fixture matrix for declared read-only, declared effectful (including remotes), undeclared mutations/wrappers, invalid/stale/protocol projections, and repair-state allow/deny including write/edit/apply_patch plus exact lint-check. Unknown tools cannot mutate through alternate names, nested schemas, wrappers, or path aliases. Declared remotes remain available in clean state and remain blocked in repair. README/matrix wording matches the exact-ID + approved repair-exception baseline. Focused and full tests pass.
notes:
## Research 2026-08-22
Citations:
- Plugin gate: `src/slopgate/resources/opencode_plugin.ts` 151-155, 456-488, 585-603
- Capability source: `src/slopgate/opencode_tool_capabilities.py` 18-81
- Installer substitution: `src/slopgate/installer/_opencode.py` 182-213
- Python second gate: `src/slopgate/adapters/opencode_projection/projector.py` 180-214
- Engine inject: `src/slopgate/engine/_evaluation.py` 111-116
- Repair mark is PostToolUse-only: `src/slopgate/engine/_evaluation.py` 42-81
- Shell alias set: `src/slopgate/util/payloads/_basic.py` 89-115
- Intent read-only names: `src/slopgate/util/payloads/_intent.py` 28-40, 225-226
- README policy: `README.md` 148
- Matrix name-search: `tests/test_opencode_hook_contract_matrix.py` 54-69
- Official hook surface: https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/

Original lexical-heuristic reproductions are historical. Do not implement schema/path walkers to "finish" this epic.
close_reason: Exact-ID OpenCode enforcement, repair parity, executable matrix, docs, runtime install, lint, and full suite are complete.

description: A post-tool finding currently affects only the current call, and sessions sharing a worktree can mutate the same files. OpenCode has one documented hard control point, tool.execute.before, which can throw before mutation, but it exposes no side-effect classification for arbitrary/custom/MCP tools. Persist repair state by worktree/repository generation, use sessionID/callID as provenance, and enforce a deny-by-default pending policy that permits only known read-only and explicit repair/verification tools. Experimental model-context transforms remain optional guidance.

Register an optional documented custom slopgate_verify_repair tool whose execute path verifies the authoritative worktree and clears only the matching generation, without depending on its own hook events. Use system transform only when sessionID is present and capability tests pass; compaction context merely restates state. app.log is diagnostic; toast is TUI-only.
acceptance_criteria: A confirmed quality violation stores REPAIR_REQUIRED for the affected worktree/repository generation with sessionID/callID provenance; all sessions sharing that worktree observe the gate while separate worktrees remain isolated; pending policy allows only known read-only and explicit repair/verification tools and denies unknown-effect tools; a documented custom verification tool can run clean verification and atomically clear only the matching generation; failed/cancelled/partial tools with no after hook cannot silently clear or avoid the gate when independent evidence recorded a violation; events never clear state; system transform skips injection when sessionID is absent and degrades safely when unavailable; compaction only restates pending context; tests cover concurrent sessions, unknown tools, calls already in flight, transform present/absent, headless mode, compaction, generation races, and every clear condition.

T2/T3: system transform is typed/wired with optional sessionID but undocumented; messages transform has no sessionID. SDK session.prompt noReply is not assumed safe recursively. Custom verification executes directly and does not rely on before/after hooks for its clear action; headless plugin-tool hook interception remains an independent unresolved regression.

title: Normalize OpenCode tool results and mutation outcomes
description:
Official OpenCode types define tool.execute.before as input {tool, sessionID, callID} plus mutable output.args, and tool.execute.after as input {tool, sessionID, callID, args} plus output {title, output, metadata}. The current shim reads nonexistent output.result and maintains an argument cache even though after receives final args directly. Normalize the documented/typed fields and represent execution and mutation outcomes without inferring success or commit from hook presence or output text.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run OpenCode 1.18.19 with the current Slopgate plugin and execute Read plus apply_patch.
2. Inspect results.jsonl for tool.execute.after rows.
3. Observe tool_output is null because the shim reads output.result instead of output.output.
4. Observe the shim caches args by tool plus cwd despite input.args, sessionID, and callID being available on the typed after hook.
design: Use the official typed hook objects directly. Mutate output.args in place before execution; hook return values are ignored. Model two independent axes: execution_outcome {returned, failed, blocked, cancelled, unknown} and mutation_outcome {committed, partial, none, unknown}, each with evidence_tier. Receiving after proves only normal return on pinned/tested versions; it never proves commit. After-output mutation is source-observed but undocumented and is not a critical delivery channel.
acceptance_criteria: The shim no longer reads output.result or uses the tool-plus-cwd argument cache on supported OpenCode versions; before uses output.args and after uses input.args plus output.title/output/output.metadata; sessionID and callID are preserved; traces store separate execution_outcome, mutation_outcome, and evidence_tier; after receipt may classify execution as returned only on pinned/tested versions and never classifies mutation as committed; absence of after remains unknown because it cannot distinguish block, failure, cancellation, or partial side effects; guidance never says an edit landed without commit evidence; tests cover normal return, thrown/absent after, in-place argument mutation, ignored return values, raw after output, and uncertain/partial mutation.
notes: Evidence tiers: T1 docs https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ and https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/#apply_patch; T2 Hooks types at anomalyco/opencode commit 3a4c253 packages/plugin/src/index.ts; T3 v1.18.19 execution wrapper commit 2b72179 packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts. Local eight-event trace recorded null output.result. apply_patch uses tool ID apply_patch and output.args.patchText per official tools docs.
close_reason: Implemented typed OpenCode before/after fields, removed argument correlation cache, preserved native IDs and raw after output, added independent execution/mutation evidence traces, and passed focused plus integration validation.

title: Repair path relocation must not escape the project root
description:
## Summary
`_locate_repair_path()` checks `is_relative_to(project)` for the original absolute path, but the suffix-relocation fallback does not. `Path.joinpath` treats an absolute first segment as a new root, so `project.joinpath(*Path('/etc/passwd').parts)` becomes `/etc/passwd`. If that file exists, verify will scan it.

## Trigger
`_locate_repair_path(Path('/tmp/project'), '/etc/passwd')` returns `/etc/passwd`.

## Do not do
Do not keep the suffix walk without a post-resolve containment check. Relative recorded paths that resolve outside the project via `..` should also be rejected (relative branch currently returns any existing `(project / candidate).resolve()`).
design: After every candidate (absolute, relocated, or relative) is resolved, require `resolved.is_file()` and `resolved.is_relative_to(project)` before returning it. Reject absolute paths that are not already inside the project rather than remapping them onto host files.
acceptance_criteria: `_locate_repair_path(project, '/etc/passwd')` and other host-absolute files return None. Relocated worktree-style prefixes still resolve to a file *inside* project. A test proves outside-project files are not added to `src_files`/`test_files` and cannot make verify succeed by scanning them.
notes: Second review 2026-08-22, finding 2. Citations: `src/slopgate/cli/repair.py` 35-48.
close_reason: Implemented root fixes and regression coverage; make test 225 passed, Ruff clean, Pyrefly 0 diagnostics, TypeScript plugin compile clean.

title: Repair verify must fail when recorded paths resolve to zero files
description:
## Summary
`_resolve_repair_files()` silently drops every path where `_locate_repair_path()` returns None. `_run_scoped_lint()` only fails when the recorded path *list* is empty; it then runs collectors on possibly empty `src_files`/`test_files`. Zero violations ⇒ exit 0 ⇒ `cmd_repair_verify()` clears the generation.

This is not covered by slopgate-8ze.1 (baseline prune of a real scoped scan) or slopgate-8ze.2 (gate=new on remaining counterparts). Here no file is inspected at all.

## Trigger
A repair generation whose only path is `src/does-not-exist.py` (deleted, malformed, or stale). Verify prints `src: (0 files)`, `✓ No violations`, and `{"status":"cleared"}`.

## Do not do
Do not treat empty resolved files as a clean lint. The existing `if not paths` guard is insufficient.
design: Fail verification before invoking collectors when recorded paths exist but resolve to zero files. Prefer fail-closed on any unresolved recorded path, not only the all-missing case. Keep the existing empty-generation message for a generation that recorded no paths at all.
acceptance_criteria: A generation with only missing/unresolvable paths fails verify, does not print a clean lint summary, and retains REPAIR_REQUIRED. A generation that records real files still verifies those files. A test covers deleted/stale recorded paths.
notes: Second review 2026-08-22, finding 1. Citations: `src/slopgate/cli/repair.py` 51-72, 88-107, 148-158. Reproduced with `src/does-not-exist.py`.
close_reason: Implemented root fixes and regression coverage; make test 225 passed, Ruff clean, Pyrefly 0 diagnostics, TypeScript plugin compile clean.

title: Repair verify must not sync or prune baselines.json
description:
## Summary
`_run_scoped_lint` calls `print_collector_results(..., gate="new")`, which always runs `_sync_baseline_after_lint`. `_lint_prune_only` is hard-coded True. Prune keeps `old ∩ current` per rule; collectors not in the scoped run count as empty current. Verifying one repaired file therefore deletes unrelated accepted debt from `baselines.json`. The next full `slopgate lint check` then reports previously accepted debt as new.

## Trigger
Verify one recorded path in a repo whose `baselines.json` has IDs for other files or other collectors.

## Do not do
Do not keep using `print_collector_results` for verify without an explicit no-sync path.
design: Repair verification must be read-only with respect to the repository baseline. Use a non-synchronizing result evaluator, or add an explicit `sync_baseline=False` path that `repair verify` always uses. Do not write `baselines.json` on success or failure.
acceptance_criteria: A scoped `repair verify` against one file/collector leaves every other baseline ID untouched. A test with pre-seeded `baselines.json` IDs for an unrecorded file asserts the file is byte-identical (or ID-identical) after verify. Existing path-scoped clear/retain tests stay green.
notes: Citations: `src/slopgate/cli/repair.py` 117-122; `src/slopgate/cli/lint/report.py` 256-338; `src/slopgate/lint/_baseline.py` 143-198. Existing `tests/test_repair_cli.py` never seeds a baseline, so this is uncaught.

title: Repair verify must fail on remaining targeted counterparts
description:
## Summary
Verify loads the existing baseline and uses `gate="new"`. A still-present counterpart whose stable ID is already baseline-known returns success, then `cmd_repair_verify()` clears the generation.

Hooks that arm repair do not consult the lint baseline. `QUALITY-LINT-001` reports every touched-file hit. `PY-CODE-015` blocks on complexity; OpenCode post-tool BLOCK/DENY arms repair via `_record_opencode_repair_required`.

## Trigger
`PY-CODE-015` or `QUALITY-LINT-001` arms repair for a function whose `high-complexity` ID is already in `baselines.json`. Invoking verify without changing the function clears the gate.

## Do not do
Do not treat this as lint-check semantics. Repair verify is a generation clear, not an agent/stop new-debt gate.
design: Evaluate targeted counterpart results with all-violation semantics. Verification fails while any targeted counterpart remains, regardless of baseline status. Depends on isolating verify from baseline sync so gate=all does not also rewrite `baselines.json`.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded path whose counterpart collector still emits a baseline-known violation fails verify and retains the generation. A clean recorded path still clears. Tests cover PY-CODE-015 → high-complexity and QUALITY-LINT-001 counterpart hits.
notes: Citations: `src/slopgate/cli/repair.py` 117-155; `src/slopgate/cli/lint/report.py` 158-163, 190-201; `src/slopgate/engine/_evaluation.py` 73-108; `src/slopgate/rules/common/quality/lint.py` 165-173; `src/slopgate/lint/_parity.py` 199, 221. Blocked by baseline-sync isolation.

title: Repair verification must not clear REPAIR_REQUIRED unsafely
description:
## Summary
Review of the OpenCode repair-verify path found defects that can clear `REPAIR_REQUIRED` without repairing the triggering problem, plus related identity/skip/TOML/cancellation gaps. Scrutiny confirmed findings 1, 2, 4–8. Finding 3 is a real design gap with a wrong trigger (QUALITY-LINT-001 already uses the same isolated scan as verify).

## Child order
1. Baseline sync isolation (P1)
2. All-violation targeted verify (P1; after or with 1)
3. Project-context verify with report-only path filter (P2; after 1–2)
4. Identity, skip-glob, TOML, cancellation, and timeout-test work can proceed in parallel with 3

## Do not do
Do not treat “clone against an unrecorded sibling” as a current QUALITY-LINT-001 arming case. The hook (`run_touched_collectors`) already uses `use_index=False` and only candidate paths.
design: Keep repair verification read-only with respect to `baselines.json`. Evaluate targeted counterpart collectors with all-violation semantics. If project-wide detectors are in scope, reuse CLI incremental context and restrict reported violations to recorded paths/collector IDs — do not restrict the analysis input set. Existing `test_repair_verify_clears_when_only_recorded_paths_are_clean` stays valid: unrelated file-local debt on unrecorded paths must still be ignored.
acceptance_criteria: Children close only when: scoped verify cannot prune or rewrite repository baseline; a still-present targeted counterpart fails verify regardless of baseline status; project-context tests use a hook-armable fixture (two recorded files or `<project>` literals), not an unrecorded sibling clone; identity/skip/TOML/cancellation/timeout tests match the child ACs. Focused repair and OpenCode plugin tests pass.

title: Avoid false-positive denial of remote OpenCode tools with path-like fields
description:
## Summary
Original bug: generic mutation verbs plus a path-like field were treated as local filesystem mutation (`github_update_issue({path: /repos/...})`). That heuristic is gone. Those IDs are now declared effectful and pass the unknown-tool gate because of the ID, not the path shape.

## Current tests
Only two clean-state allows:
- `github_update_issue({path: /repos/o/r/issues/1})`
- `api_delete_resource({path: /v1/items/1})`
in `test_engine.py::_REMOTE_EFFECT_TOOLS` and `test_opencode_plugin_control_contract.py::_REMOTE_EFFECT_TOOL_CASES`.

## Remaining gap
Add the same declared-remote IDs with `source`, `target`, `url`, and `file:` URI values, plus matching *undeclared* IDs with those fields (must still deny). In REPAIR_REQUIRED, declared remotes must deny (`isAllowedWhileRepairRequired` does not include them).

## Do not do
Do not add local-vs-remote path parsing. That is how the original false positive was created and it cannot be made safe for `/repos/...` vs `/tmp/...` vs `file:` URIs.
design:
Trust declared effectful IDs. Argument shape is irrelevant to the hard gate.

Test matrix (after `slopgate-nvz.3`):
- Declared remote + path/source/target/url/file-URI => clean-state allow (engine/rules may still apply; `OC-PROJECTION-001` must not fire).
- Undeclared ID + the same fields => deny unknown effect.
- Declared remote during REPAIR_REQUIRED => repair denial.
- Declared local mutator with equivalent field names still projects/blocks via projection status, not path heuristics.

README must say remotes are available only when declared, and are blocked during repair.
acceptance_criteria: Declared remote IDs remain available in clean state for path, source, target, URL, and file-URI argument shapes. Undeclared IDs with those shapes remain denied. Local declared mutations still block through projection, not path tokens. Repair-mode denies declared remotes. README matches. No local-vs-remote path heuristic is added.
notes: Citations: `EFFECTFUL_TOOL_IDS` includes `github_update_issue` and `api_delete_resource`; plugin repair allowlist is only read-only + write/edit/apply_patch + verify/lint-check. Blocked by `slopgate-nvz.3`.
close_reason: Covered declared remote effects across path-like schemas without path heuristics.

title: Path-scope slopgate_verify_repair instead of full-repo lint check
description:
## Why

`slopgate_verify_repair` clears OpenCode `REPAIR_REQUIRED` by running `slopgate repair verify`, which shells out to full-repo `slopgate lint check` (`LINT_SCOPE_ALL`). Repair state already stores `generation`, `paths`, and `rule_ids`. Verify ignores those and scans the entire project.

On job-hunter that is ~1898 src + ~2271 test files. Successful clears take ~81s. A 2026-08-22 Hephaestus session (`ses_fd6f014a9ffesovCQiJJZSsCaQ`) armed generation `9a673560…` for `PY-CODE-015` on three files, then wedged for 10+ minutes in `python -m slopgate lint check` at 100% CPU (one worker ~95% `Rl`). OpenCode logged no loop events after 12:39:01Z because `callRepairCommand` has no timeout. The agent retried every 2–4 minutes (eight orphaned `PreToolUse` with no `PostToolUse`). Session was aborted/deleted and PIDs 1622493/1622502 killed.

Full-repo `lint check` must stay the stop/agent gate. It must not be the per-generation repair unlock.

## What to do

Change the clear contract so verify lints the generation's recorded paths (and those rule IDs), then atomically clears only that generation. Reuse incremental/changed-scope lint. Do not weaken `lint check`. Keep generation-checked clears; do not clear on cancel or timeout.
design:
## Contract

- Authoritative unlock: `clear_repair_required(generation)` only after a clean result for that generation's `paths` + `rule_ids`.
- `slopgate lint check` remains full-repo / `LINT_SCOPE_ALL` for stop/agent quality. Do not change that command's scope.
- New or extended path: `repair verify` (and the OpenCode custom tool) runs path-scoped / incremental lint against stored repair paths.
- Reuse existing incremental / `LINT_SCOPE_CHANGED` collectors. Do not add a second scanner.
- Generation mismatch still returns status `generation_mismatch` and does not clear.
- Timeout, cancel, or failed scoped lint leaves `REPAIR_REQUIRED` in place.

## Plugin

- `callRepairCommand` must timeout, kill the process group, and return structured JSON (`timeout` / `failed`).
- Single-flight per worktree+generation: join or reject stacked `slopgate_verify_repair` calls.
- OpenCode abort/cancel must kill the lint child so retries do not pile up.

## Out of scope

- Raising timeouts and keeping full-repo verify.
- Clearing repair because a tool was cancelled or "probably clean".
- Changing unknown-tool enforcement (owned by slopgate-nvz).
acceptance_criteria:
- `repair verify` for a generation lints only that generation's recorded paths/rule IDs, not `LINT_SCOPE_ALL`.
- A clean scoped result clears only the matching generation; a dirty result, timeout, cancel, or generation mismatch leaves the gate set.
- Full-repo `slopgate lint check` still forces repo-root all-scope and remains the stop/agent gate.
- Concurrent `slopgate_verify_repair` calls for the same generation do not start a second full scan.
- Plugin timeout/cancel kills the verify/lint process group and returns structured failure without wedging OpenCode.
- Tests cover path-scoped clean clear, dirty retain, generation mismatch, timeout/cancel retain, and unchanged full-repo lint check behavior.
notes: Implemented path-scoped repair verify: collectors run only on recorded generation paths/rule IDs; lint check stays LINT_SCOPE_ALL. Plugin callRepairCommand now timeouts, kills the process group, single-flights per worktree+generation, and returns structured timeout/cancelled/failed JSON.
close_reason: Path-scoped repair verify + plugin timeout/single-flight implemented and tested.

title: Use native OpenCode identity and eliminate arg/cwd correlation state
description:
OpenCode's typed tool hooks already provide sessionID and callID, and tool.execute.after provides final args. Plugin initialization provides stable directory and worktree. Tool-hook inputs and generic event envelopes do not provide cwd. Replace synthetic canonical identity, mutable currentDirectory, and tool-plus-cwd argument caching with the native contract; parse event identity from event.properties and the file.edited path from properties.file.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start concurrent OpenCode sessions or subagents in one plugin instance and invoke the same tool.
2. Inspect hook inputs and Slopgate traces.
3. Observe native sessionID/callID/final args exist but the shim records one generated session ID and correlates via tool plus mutable cwd.
4. Emit file.edited and observe the official properties.file key is not among the shim path keys.
design: For typed hooks, pass input.sessionID, input.callID, and input.args/output.args directly. Use plugin-context directory/worktree as the authoritative filesystem scope and shell.env.cwd only on that typed hook. Repair state is keyed by worktree/repository or affected-path generation; sessionID/callID are provenance, not isolation boundaries. For generic events read fields from event.properties. Delete mutable cwd and argument-cache state rather than re-keying it.
acceptance_criteria: Tool hooks use native sessionID/callID and direct typed args with no tool/cwd cache; canonical repo scope uses plugin directory/worktree and never undocumented input.cwd or event.cwd; authoritative repair state is shared by sessions operating on the same worktree and isolated across different worktrees; concurrent state changes are generation-checked or atomic; shell.env may supply cwd only from its typed input; generic events read session identity from properties and file.edited reads properties.file; compatibility/native duplicates are deduplicated without collapsing distinct calls or worktrees.
notes: Evidence: official Plugins docs document plugin context directory/worktree; official Hooks types expose sessionID/callID and after input.args but no cwd on tool hooks; Event is {id,type,properties}; v1.18.19 source filters events to the plugin directory before delivery. Current local shim lines 118-147, 306-352, and 425+ use generated identity/cache/mutable cwd.

title: Use typed OpenCode hooks for control and generic events for telemetry
description:
OpenCode generic event handlers return Promise<void> but v1.18.19/current source invokes them fire-and-forget; they cannot block originating work or safely author ordered lifecycle transitions. The event envelope is {id,type,properties}. Slopgate currently attempts enforcement from file.edited and treats several event fields as top-level. Reserve hard control for documented tool.execute.before and use generic events only for append-only telemetry, provisional mutation evidence, lifecycle observations, and human notification.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Perform a file mutation that emits file.edited and a blocking quality result.
2. Trace the generic event handler and upstream dispatch.
3. Observe upstream discards the event promise while Slopgate throws from the event path.
4. Observe official event data is nested under properties and file.edited uses properties.file.
design: Never throw from event. Catch and log event-handler failures. Generic events are append-only telemetry and provisional evidence: they cannot clear repair state, supersede newer verification, or author authoritative lifecycle transitions without generation reconciliation. Use typed, wired tool.execute.before for control; do not rely on permission.ask because it is declared but has no trigger site. Treat permission event names as version-sensitive. Keep file.edited as delayed directory-scoped evidence, not rollback or denial.
acceptance_criteria: Generic event handling is telemetry/advisory only and never throws for policy control; event fields are read from properties, including file.edited.file and session IDs; rejected or reordered event work is caught and logged; event evidence is generation-tagged and cannot clear or overwrite authoritative repair state; hard mutation control is owned by tool.execute.before; no path depends on permission.ask or one permission event spelling; capability docs distinguish typed chat.message from a documented prompt blocker; tests prove event-side findings do not masquerade as tool denial, do not clear newer state, and preserve provisional mutation evidence.
notes: T1 docs list generic events and use them for notifications. T2 Event handler returns Promise<void>. T3 v1.18.19 commit 2b72179 and current dev 3a4c253 invoke void hook.event after directory filtering. permission.ask is typed but an exhaustive source scan found no trigger site; permission event names diverge across docs and schemas.
close_reason: Typed tool.execute.before remains the hard control point; generic events now catch/log failures, file.edited is advisory provisional evidence, docs clarify prompt/permission limitations, and Bun plus state/trace contract tests pass.

title: OpenCode TOML scope parser must accept header comments
description:
## Summary
`tomlDisablesRepo` recognizes a table header only when `]` ends the line. Valid TOML such as `[slopgate] # local override` leaves `section` unset, so a following `enabled = false` is ignored. Python `is_repo_disabled` uses a real TOML parse and treats the repo as relaxed. The plugin then stays strict and can hard-deny unknown tools or apply the repair gate before Python runs.

## Trigger
`[slopgate] # local override` plus `enabled = false` in `slopgate.toml`.
design: Accept trailing TOML comments on table headers, or replace the partial parser with one that matches the supported configuration grammar. Key-line comments (`enabled = false # …`) already work and must stay working.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin `enforcementModeFor` returns `repo_relaxed` for `[slopgate] # comment` + `enabled = false`, matching Python. A Bun/plugin test covers the commented header. Uncommented `[slopgate]` and sentinel files still work.
notes: Citations: `src/slopgate/resources/opencode_plugin.ts` 368-398; `src/slopgate/config/_repo.py` 208-224.

title: Decouple repair verify single-flight from first caller abort
description:
## Summary
`verifyRepairFlight` stores one promise created with the first caller’s `AbortSignal`. Later callers join it but their signals are ignored. Aborting the first caller kills verification for every waiter; aborting a later waiter does nothing.

## Trigger
Two sessions in the same OpenCode process verify the same worktree generation; the initiating session is cancelled. Scope is one in-process `verifyFlights` map (`cwd::generation`), not two separate OpenCode processes.
design: Decouple the shared subprocess lifetime from individual waiters, or reference-count waiters and kill only when all have cancelled. A first-caller timeout must not be treated as a successful clear for remaining waiters.
acceptance_criteria: A test with two concurrent verify calls shows: aborting the first waiter does not fail the still-active waiter with `cancelled`, and aborting a later waiter does not kill the shared scan while another waiter remains. Same-generation join still starts only one subprocess.
notes: Citations: `src/slopgate/resources/opencode_plugin.ts` 171, 483-568, 801-810.
close_reason: Implemented root fixes and regression coverage; make test 225 passed, Ruff clean, Pyrefly 0 diagnostics, TypeScript plugin compile clean.

title: slopgate check skip_paths must match runtime and status policy
description:
## Summary
Two related CLI/runtime disagreements:

1. Relative skip globs are anchored to the inspected target (dir or file parent) in `_check_skip_state`, while the engine uses `ctx.cwd`. `skip_paths = ["generated/*"]` plus `slopgate check /repo/generated/output.py` becomes `/repo/generated/generated/*`, so `target_path_skipped` is false when runtime would skip.

2. Status only consults `target_skipped`. `repo_skipped` can be true while `status` is still `ENROLLED`, so the report contradicts itself (`target_path_skipped: false`, `repo_path_skipped: true`, `status: ENROLLED`).

## Triggers
- Relative: `generated/*` vs `slopgate check /repo/generated/output.py` → reported `[false, false]`, expected target skip true.
- Repo-level skip: `repo_skipped=true` with `status=ENROLLED`.

## Precision
Enforcement is cwd-relative (`base_dir=ctx.cwd`), not strictly `resolved_repo_root`. Anchoring check to `resolved_repo_root` is still the right CLI default; it is slightly stricter than the hook when cwd is a subdirectory.
design: Use the same base directory as runtime evaluation: `resolved_repo_root` when enrolled, otherwise the target base. Define whether a repository-level skip makes top-level `status` `SKIPPED` (recommended: yes, so `status` cannot be ENROLLED while `repo_path_skipped` is true). Test both glob anchoring and the status policy explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: `slopgate check /repo/generated/output.py` with `skip_paths = [\"generated/*\"]` reports `target_path_skipped=true` when `/repo` is enrolled. A repo-level skip cannot report `status=ENROLLED` together with `repo_path_skipped=true`; status is `SKIPPED` or the fields are documented and tested as a deliberate split. Unenrolled targets still resolve relative patterns against the target base. Engine skip behavior is unchanged unless this ticket explicitly expands.
notes:
Citations: `src/slopgate/cli/check.py` 25-38; `src/slopgate/config/_repo.py` 227-249; `src/slopgate/engine/_runner.py` 261-273.
Second review 2026-08-22, finding 3: status uses only `target_skipped` (`check.py` 49-56), so `repo_path_skipped=true` can coexist with `status=ENROLLED`. Not a new ticket — same skip-state function.

title: Repair verify should keep project analysis context
description:
## Summary
Verify passes only recorded files and disables index/constants (`use_index=False`, `build_constants=False`). Cross-file collectors cannot reconstruct a project-wide hit from that input.

The original review trigger is a misconception: `QUALITY-LINT-001` already calls `run_touched_collectors` with the same isolation, so a clone against an unrecorded sibling would not arm repair today. Repo tests also want path-scoped verify to ignore unrelated file-local debt (`huge.py`).

## Real holes
- Repair records `content_targets`; QUALITY-LINT-001 scans `candidate_paths` and treats `<project>` as in-scope. A multi-file or project-literal hit can be armed from a wider set than verify rescans.
- CLI incremental (`lint check`) keeps full inventory + index; verify does not.

## Do not do
Do not add a regression whose violation requires a second unrecorded file as a QUALITY-LINT-001 arming case. That fixture cannot fire the hook today.
design: Reuse CLI changed/incremental scope that retains project-wide analysis context, then restrict *reported* violations to recorded paths and collector IDs. Do not restrict the analysis input set. `test_repair_verify_clears_when_only_recorded_paths_are_clean` stays valid.
acceptance_criteria: A hook-armable fixture (two recorded files, or `<project>` literals in candidate/content scope) still fails verify until the counterpart is gone. Unrelated file-local debt on unrecorded paths does not block clear. No test claims an unrecorded sibling clone arms QUALITY-LINT-001.
notes: Citations: `src/slopgate/cli/repair.py` 98-106; `src/slopgate/lint/_collector_groups/runners.py` 56-75; `src/slopgate/rules/common/quality/lint.py` 86-173; `src/slopgate/engine/_evaluation.py` 78; `tests/test_repair_cli.py` 222-235. Do after baseline-sync isolation and all-violation gate.

title: Preflight projected quality for supported OpenCode edits
description: Post-tool rejection cannot undo a mutation. OpenCode officially documents tool.execute.before as an in-place argument mutation and throw-to-block surface, and its tools docs specify apply_patch arguments under output.args.patchText. For deterministic mutation tools, construct projected content before execution, run applicable quality checks, and throw only when the projection is trustworthy; retain post-edit observation for everything else.
design: Use documented output.args and exact versioned tool schemas. Start with apply_patch.patchText and other payloads whose resulting content can be reconstructed without filesystem races. Preflight classification is separate from the pending repair gate: while repair is pending, unknown-effect tools are denied unless explicitly allowlisted. Never rely on permission.ask. Unsupported operations fall back to post-tool observation with mutation unknown; file.edited is provisional evidence and cannot clear state. The dedicated verification tool owns authoritative clean clearing.
acceptance_criteria: Supported tool IDs and schemas are versioned, including apply_patch.patchText; deterministic projections do not touch disk and can deny through documented before-hook throw; projections verify current state; unsupported, dynamic, invalid, concurrent-change, custom, MCP, and unknown-effect operations never receive a false safe classification and are denied while a hard repair gate is pending unless explicitly allowlisted; preflight and post-tool findings deduplicate by stable generation-aware identity; tests cover valid/invalid/multi-file apply_patch, write/edit schemas, concurrent changes, unknown tools, missing after after partial side effects, and post-tool fallback; only the dedicated clean verification path may clear repair state; docs state after/file.edited cannot roll back.
notes: T1 evidence: https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/#env-protection and https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/#apply_patch. T3 confirms before executes before item.execute and after after mutation for v1.18.19/current dev. permission.ask is intentionally excluded because it has no trigger site despite its type declaration.
close_reason: Implemented versioned OpenCode mutation projection and fail-closed repair enforcement; full automated validation and live clean/pending/stale/success/corrupt CLI QA passed.

title: Timeout verify test must assert generation is retained
description:

Do not weaken the timeout assertion. Add state, do not rename the test to hide the gap.
